correctness.rationale: The published forward formulas reduce, in chord coordinates, to \(x=(v-u)/(uv)\) and \(y=(v-u)/((L-u)(L-v))\). For arbitrary positive \(x,y\), midpoint/half-length variables reduce inversion to one strictly increasing scalar equation with range \((0,\infty)\), giving existence and uniqueness. The exact Jacobian is negative because \(L(u+v)-2uv=u(L-v)+v(L-u)>0\).

value.rationale: The feasible-data set is a natural exact invariant of the simplest masking-function inverse problem. Classifying it as the entire positive quadrant turns a uniqueness statement into a complete existence-and-uniqueness theorem, provides a constructive scalar inverse, and supplies an exact Jacobian for sensitivity analysis. This is a motivated complete classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
